title: The Marketing Team
subtitle: How to talk about roles and people on a marketing team
description: Learn the words for jobs and roles on a marketing team and how to say simply what each person does.
dialogueSubtitle: Riley tells Dana about the people on the Brightline marketing team

vocabulary.definition: A person who is in charge of a team or part of a company.
vocabulary.example: The marketing manager looks after the whole marketing team.

vocabulary.definition: A person with a senior job who makes big decisions for the company.
vocabulary.example: The marketing director is in charge of all marketing at Brightline.

vocabulary.definition: A person who works in marketing and helps plan and run campaigns.
vocabulary.example: The marketing executive helps plan campaigns for the brand.

vocabulary.definition: A student or new worker who works at a company for a short time to learn.
vocabulary.example: Our intern is helping us with social media this month.

vocabulary.definition: A company that helps other companies with their marketing.
vocabulary.example: We work with an agency for our online advertising.

vocabulary.definition: A person who helps someone else with their work.
vocabulary.example: The marketing assistant helps the team with day-to-day tasks.

vocabulary.definition: The person in charge of a department or team.
vocabulary.example: Sam is the head of marketing — everyone in the team reports to her.
My colleague Carlos looks after the company's social media.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Say that someone is responsible for a team or area of work.
phrasalVerbs.example: The marketing manager is in charge of all campaigns and content.
The marketing executive reports to the marketing manager.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Say that someone is responsible for something.
phrasalVerbs.example: My colleague looks after our social media accounts.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Say that a person or team works together with someone else.
phrasalVerbs.example: Our team works with an agency for our paid advertising.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Say what area of work a person owns or manages.
phrasalVerbs.example: The director is responsible for the whole marketing department.

phrasalVerbs.definition: The normal work that someone does every day.
phrasalVerbs.example: My day to day work is writing content and looking after social media.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Can you tell me a bit about your team, Riley?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Of course. At the top we have Sarah — she is the marketing [[director:a person with a senior job who makes big decisions for the company]]. She is in charge of the whole department.

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: That is James — our marketing [[manager:a person who is in charge of a team or part of a company]]. He looks after the day to day work and all the campaigns.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: And where do you fit in the team?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: I am a marketing [[executive:a person who works in marketing and helps plan and run campaigns]]. I report to James. I help plan campaigns and write content.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Is there anyone else on the team?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Yes — we have a marketing [[assistant:a person who helps someone else with their work]], Leo. He helps with day to day tasks like emails and reports.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: What about an [[intern:a student or new worker who works at a company for a short time to learn]]?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Yes! We have an intern this month — she is helping my [[colleague:a person you work with]] Carlos with social media.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Do you work with an [[agency:a company that helps other companies with their marketing]] too?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: We do — we work with an agency for our paid ads. They report to James and work closely with the team.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: It sounds like a well-organised team. Who is the [[head:the person in charge of a department or team]] of the whole department?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: That is Sarah — the director. Everyone reports to her in the end.

chooseResponse.instructions: Work in groups. Read the question. Talk about which answer (A, B, or C) is best. Choose together, then click to check.

items.customerLine: Who is in charge of your marketing team?
options: Our marketing director, Sarah, is in charge of the whole department. Everyone reports to her.
There are many people in charge.
items.explanation: B is correct. It gives the name, the job title, and says clearly that everyone reports to her. A does not say who the director is. C is not clear and does not give any useful information.

items.customerLine: What do you do in your team?
options: I am a marketing executive. I help plan campaigns and write content. I report to the marketing manager.
items.explanation: B is correct. It gives your job title, what you do, and who you report to — a clear picture of your role. A is too vague. C says almost nothing useful.

items.customerLine: Do you have an intern on the team?
options: Yes — she is helping my colleague Carlos with social media this month.
I'm not sure — I think so.
items.explanation: A is correct. It says yes, says what the intern is doing, and says who she is working with. B says very little and sounds unsure. C sounds like you do not know your own team.

items.customerLine: Do you use an agency or do you do everything in-house?
options: Both — our team looks after content and campaigns, and we work with an agency for our paid advertising.
items.explanation: A is correct. It says what the team does and what the agency does — a clear answer that shows you know how the team works. B says too little. C avoids giving a real answer.

profileMatch.instructions: You are Riley. Three people ask about your team. As a group, talk about which way to describe the team fits each situation best. Click 'Check Matches' when you agree.

profiles.name: A new client on a first call
profiles.description: A client wants to know who they will be working with. They want to know the main people and what each person does.

profiles.name: A new intern starting this week
profiles.description: A new intern has just joined the team. They want to understand how the team is set up and who to go to for different things.

profiles.name: A contact at a networking event
profiles.description: Someone at an event asks how big your team is. They are curious but not a client. You have about 30 seconds.

options.label: Name and role
options.description: Say the name and job title of each key person, and one sentence about what they do. Best when a client needs to know who to contact and why.

options.label: Top to bottom
options.description: Start at the top — the director — and go down through the team one by one. Say who reports to who. Best when someone new needs to understand how the team is set up.

options.label: One short answer
options.description: Say the team size and one or two things about what the team does. No names or job titles needed. Best for a quick, casual conversation.

finishTheLine.instructions: The marketer's line is not finished. As a group, talk about how you would finish it. Use words from this lesson. There is no one right answer — share your ideas, then click to see one example.

items.customerLine: Can you describe your team structure?
items.salespersonStart: Of course — at the top we have Sarah, the marketing director. She is in charge of the whole department.
items.suggestedCompletion: Below her is James, the marketing manager. He looks after the day to day work. Then there is me — I am an executive — and Leo, our assistant. We also have an intern and we work with an agency for paid advertising.

items.customerLine: Who would I contact if I have a question about the campaign?
items.salespersonStart: For most questions, you can come to me — I am the executive working on your account. But if it is a big
items.suggestedCompletion: decision, James is the marketing manager and he is in charge of all campaigns. He reports to Sarah, the director, for anything at a senior level.

items.customerLine: Does your team do all the work, or do you use outside help?
items.salespersonStart: We do most things in-house — the team looks after content, campaigns, and social media. But we also work with an
items.suggestedCompletion: agency for our paid advertising. They work closely with James and report to him on all the ad campaigns.

items.customerLine: What does a marketing executive actually do?
items.salespersonStart: A marketing executive helps plan and run campaigns. Day to day, you might be
items.suggestedCompletion: writing content, setting up ads, or looking at data to see how a campaign is going. You report to the marketing manager and work closely with the rest of the team.
